# Gash itself: reference

Help, the doctor, prerequisites, settings, updates and removal. The guide is [README.md](README.md); this page lists every command, shortcut and alias, as their own help prints it (`gash help NAME`, `gash COMMAND --help`).

### gash

The overview of Gash: namespaces, their commands and shortcuts.

#### Usage

```text
gash [NAMESPACE|all] [--no-color]
gash NAMESPACE COMMAND [ARGS...]

gash                 The overview: namespaces and Gash's own commands
gash NAMESPACE       Its commands (usage, shortcut, description) and shortcuts
gash all             Every namespace page
```

#### Namespaces

```text
files, system, shell, git, docker, remote, db, runtime, ai,
hte, wsl, win, logs, llm, agent
(the former card topics nav, navigation, dev, php and node still open
their namespace page)

The pages are built from the command tree and the alias files. In an
interactive shell they list only the shortcuts the shell defines (one
skipped because a program of that name exists, or a pack whose tool is
missing, is left out); headless they list them all.
```

#### Examples

```bash
# The git commands and shortcuts
gash git

# The Docker commands
gash docker

# Every page, plain text for a file
gash all --no-color > gash-pages.txt

# Run a command by its canonical name
gash files largest --limit 5
```

See also: [`gash_help`](../gash/reference.md#gash-help), [`gash_doctor`](../gash/reference.md#gash-doctor)

### gash config init

Create ~/.gash_env configuration template.

Former name: `gash_env_init` (with `GASH_LEGACY_NAMES=1`).

#### Usage

```text
gash config init [--force]
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Create config from template (will not overwrite existing)
gash config init

# Overwrite existing config with fresh template
gash config init --force
```

#### Notes

```text
Creates ~/.gash_env with template sections for:
  SSH:~/.ssh/id_ed25519=your_passphrase
  DB:default=mysql://user:pass@host:port/db
  AI:claude=sk-ant-api03-xxxxx
Always set permissions: chmod 600 ~/.gash_env
```

See also: [`gash db list`](../databases/reference.md#gash-db-list), [`gash ai providers`](../ai/reference.md#gash-ai-providers), [`gash remote unlock-keys`](../remote/reference.md#gash-remote-unlock-keys)

### gash doctor

Run health checks on the Gash installation.

Shortcut: `gdoctor`. Former name: `gash_doctor` (with `GASH_LEGACY_NAMES=1`).

#### Usage

```text
gash doctor [--timing] [--no-color] [--prereqs] [--json]
gash doctor --install [--yes] [--all] [TOOL...]
gash doctor --legacy [--json] [FILE...]
```

#### Options

```text
--timing    What each file and step costs when a shell starts
--no-color  Plain output
--prereqs   Only the prerequisites: every external tool, by area
--json      The prerequisites as one JSON object, for scripts and agents
--install   Install the missing tools (or the TOOLs named) with the
            system's package manager, after asking
--yes, -y   With --install: do not ask
--all       With --install: the optional tools too
--legacy    The former flat names of Gash 3.x (gash files largest) that the
            FILEs call, with the command that replaces each; without
            FILE, the startup files of your home (~/.bashrc,
            ~/.bash_local and the others)
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Run a full health check
gash doctor

# What is missing on this system, and how to install it
gash doctor --prereqs

# Install rsync and ssh with the package manager (asks first)
gash doctor --install rsync ssh

# Find what makes new shells slow
gash doctor --timing

# Which lines of a script still call a Gash 3.x name
gash doctor --legacy ~/bin/backup.sh
```

#### Notes

```text
Checks: core files, modules, the binary and gash-hosts-helper
(against the hashes release/SHA256SUMS pins), the generated
shims (against this gash version), config file permissions, the
SSH keys of ~/.gash_env, and every external tool Gash runs, with
the package and the install command for this system (apt, dnf,
pacman, zypper, apk or brew). A missing required tool is an
issue; a tool only some functions need is a warning.
Returns 1 when a check fails (2 for an unknown option).

--install never runs for an agent (GASH_HEADLESS=1): it answers
with the install_needs_confirmation error and the command to show
the user. Without a terminal to ask on it needs --yes. Docker
and nvm are never installed: their line links the official
instructions.

--timing loads Gash in a new interactive shell and lists the
milliseconds each file and step takes (5 ms or more stands out),
then times whole new shells: with your ~/.bashrc, and bash alone,
3 times each (a line says first that your ~/.bashrc runs 3 times).
Needs Bash 5.0 or newer. Starting a shell with GASH_TIMING=1 keeps
the same figures in its __GASH_LOAD_TIMES array.

--legacy reads text, not Bash: a name in a string counts, a
comment line does not. It returns 1 when it finds a name or
cannot read a FILE. Gash 4 defines the former names only with
GASH_LEGACY_NAMES=1; an interactive shell whose startup files
call one says so on stderr, at most once a day.
```

See also: `gash update`, [`gash`](../gash/reference.md#gash)

### gash help

The page of a command, a namespace or a topic; search every page.

Former name: `gash_help` (with `GASH_LEGACY_NAMES=1`).

#### Usage

```text
gash help                    The overview: namespaces and Gash's own commands
gash help NAME               The page of a command, shortcut or former name
gash help NAMESPACE          The commands of a namespace (gash help git)
gash help TOPIC              shortcuts, shell-defaults, scripting, migrate
gash help --list             Every command, by namespace
gash help --search WORD      Search every page
gash help --short NAME       One-line description (for scripting)
gash help --bash TOPIC       Bash builtin help (e.g. cd, export)
```

#### Examples

```bash
# The page of a command
gash help ai query

# By its shortcut or its former name
gash help flf
gash help files_largest

# Every command that mentions Docker
gash help --search docker

# Every shortcut this shell defines
gash help shortcuts

# Just the description, for scripting
gash help --short files largest

# Bash builtin help
gash help --bash cd
```

See also: [`gash`](../gash/reference.md#gash)

### gash shell username

Print the current user name.

Also `gash_username`, a function prompts and scripts call.

#### Usage

```text
gash shell username
```

#### Examples

```bash
# The name the banner and the prompt show
gash shell username
```

#### Notes

```text
Tries whoami, then id -un, then the /etc/passwd entry of the
current user id; prints UNKNOWN_USERNAME when all of them fail.
```

### gash uninstall

Uninstall Gash and clean up configurations.

Former name: `gash_uninstall` (with `GASH_LEGACY_NAMES=1`).

#### Usage

```text
gash uninstall
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Remove Gash completely (interactive confirmation)
gash uninstall
```

#### Notes

```text
Removes the Gash sourcing block from your shell profile,
deletes the installation directory, and cleans up.
Kept as FILE.gash-uninstall.bak: each profile as it was
before the edit, and a ~/.gashrc that holds your own lines.
Restart your terminal after uninstalling.
```

See also: `gash update`, [`gash unload`](../gash/reference.md#gash-unload)

### gash unload

Restore shell state to before Gash was loaded.

Former name: `gash_unload` (with `GASH_LEGACY_NAMES=1`).

#### Usage

```text
gash unload
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Temporarily disable Gash in the current terminal
gash unload

# Re-enable Gash without restarting
source ~/.gashrc
```

#### Notes

```text
Removes all functions, aliases, and settings introduced by Gash.
Restores PS1, PROMPT_COMMAND, history settings, and shopt options
to the state captured before Gash loaded. Session-only: does not
modify any files.
```

See also: [`gash uninstall`](../gash/reference.md#gash-uninstall)

### gash update

Upgrade Gash to the latest version.

Former name: `gash_upgrade` (with `GASH_LEGACY_NAMES=1`).

#### Usage

```text
gash update
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Upgrade to latest version
gash update
# Then restart your terminal to apply changes
```

#### Notes

```text
Fetches the release tags and checks out the newest release (never
an older one). It runs the steps of gash update. A checkout newer
than the latest release (a pre-release, or a commit after it) is
left as it is.
Before the checkout, the release binary is downloaded into
~/.local/share/gash/versions/<version>/ and verified (the hash in
the tag's release/SHA256SUMS, else the release's checksums.txt;
GASH_REQUIRE_SIGNED=1 also requires a signed tag or a Sigstore
release signature that cosign verifies, and a pinned binary).
After it, the new version is loaded in a test shell; if that
fails, the previous version is checked out again.
Open a new terminal afterwards to load the new version.
To go back: gash update --rollback (the previous version and its
binary are kept), or git -C ~/.gash checkout vX.Y.Z
```

See also: [`gash doctor`](../gash/reference.md#gash-doctor), [`gash uninstall`](../gash/reference.md#gash-uninstall)

### gash_migrate

Shows how to migrate a Gash 1.x configuration.

#### Usage

```text
gash_migrate
(also: gash migrate)

Gash 3 does not migrate a Gash 1.x configuration. gash_migrate prints
one line on stderr with the route and returns 1: check out v2.1.0 in
your Gash directory, open a new terminal, run gash_migrate there (the
2.x guided review, with a diff preview and backups), then gash_upgrade.
It writes nothing.

While ~/.gashrc is still the 1.x loader, an interactive shell prints a
one-line reminder on stderr, at most once a day. Headless shells print
nothing.
```

#### Files

```text
~/.local/state/gash/schema     configuration schema version (2 or more:
                               no reminder)
~/.local/state/gash/notice     time of the last reminder
(under $XDG_STATE_HOME/gash when that is set)
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Show the route
gash migrate
```

See also: `gash gash_doctor gash_upgrade`

## Command trees

### gash version

```text
Print the version, platform and path of this binary

Usage:
  gash version [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for version
      --json   print one JSON object
```

### gash init

```text
Print the interactive Bash layer for gash.sh to evaluate

Usage:
  gash init bash [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for init
```

### gash update

```text
Update the Gash install (~/.gash, or $GASH_DIR) to the highest release tag
of its origin, verified before anything changes:

  1. refuses a working tree with local modifications;
  2. fetches the tags and picks the highest release (never an older one
     than the checkout: a pre-release or a later commit stays as it is);
  3. checks the tag signature, or for an unsigned tag the Sigstore
     signature of its release with cosign (GASH_REQUIRE_SIGNED=1 refuses
     a tag with neither verified);
  4. downloads the release binary into
     ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/gash/versions/<version>/ and checks it
     against the hash the tagged tree pins (release/SHA256SUMS), else the
     release's checksums.txt (GASH_REQUIRE_SIGNED=1 accepts only a pinned
     binary); the binary must answer "gash version --json" with that version;
  5. checks out the tag and loads it in two new shells (headless and
     interactive); if either fails, the previous version is checked out
     again, its binary still installed.

The previous version and its binary are kept: "gash update --rollback"
returns to it (and a second rollback comes back). gash_upgrade runs the same
steps. GASH_RELEASE_URL replaces the release download URL (file:// works).

Exit status: 0 updated or nothing to do, 1 refused or failed (nothing
changed, or the previous version restored), 2 a bad argument.

Usage:
  gash update [--rollback] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help       help for update
      --rollback   return to the version the last update left
```
